tool_input.command:
git add CHANGELOG.md DESIGN.md internal/audit/scan_test.go internal/audit/seal.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(audit): AppendMonotonic truncates back on a write or sync failure (P1, PR #509 tail #3)

Checked first, per the leader's instruction: internal/mission/log.go's
existing truncate-on-short-write path does NOT cover this case. That
path lives in appendEventLocked's legacy (single-tree) branch, which
never calls Sync at all, and which every two-tree (current, in-repo)
mission bypasses entirely -- routed instead to internal/audit's
AppendMonotonic, which had no rollback of any kind: a Write succeeding
followed by a failing Sync still left the line on disk, fsync failure
or not.

Store.DisclaimDelegation (and appendEventLocked's other ten call
sites) treats a returned append error as proof nothing new persisted,
and DisclaimDelegation specifically restores the delegation record to
its pre-disclaim bytes on that belief. With the gap open, a sync
failure during disclaim's event append left the log genuinely showing
the disclaim happened while the record said it hadn't, and a retry
would append a second disclaim_delegation line for the same event.

AppendMonotonic now captures the pre-write file length and truncates
back to it on any write failure/short write OR a sync failure, mirroring
the legacy path's write-failure discipline and extending it to the sync
case the legacy path never needed. Sync itself now runs through a new
fsyncFile package var (mirrors internal/mission/syncdir_unix.go's
syncDir) so tests can inject a failure a real fsync failure is not
portable to engineer.

No change needed in DisclaimDelegation or any other caller -- the fix
is entirely in the shared primitive.

Confirmed both new tests red first against a bare pre-fix Sync-failure
return (no Truncate call): the line persisted despite the reported
failure, and a retry produced two lines instead of one.

make check green (race detector included); GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64
go build ./... exits 0.
EOF
)"
